rounds.method_summary: Baseline dead-zone (τ=0.6) verified: bpp=0.020130, dists=0.122199, matches anchors exactly. Collected y_res/scales stats: ~98-99% zero after rounding, y_abs_mean≈0.05-0.08, scale_mean≈0.12. 128 channels at 32x48 spatial.

Per-latent RDOQ with ±1 candidates, λ=0.055. Matches reference exactly: bpp=0.020194, dists=0.119769, score=0.5849. Baseline bpp=0.020130 with headroom to cap=0.020231 (0.000037 bpp = 0.18% available).

RDOQ ±2 candidates, λ=0.06. bpp=0.019982 (way under cap 0.020231), dists=0.12143 (worse than reference 0.11977), score=0.185. λ too high → under-utilizing bit budget. Need λ≈0.053 to hit bpp cap with ±2 candidates.

RDOQ ±2 candidates, λ=0.053. bpp=0.02025 OVER cap (0.020231) → score=0. But dists=0.11905 is better than reference 0.11977, showing ±2 has potential. Need to increase λ slightly to ~0.054 to get under cap while keeping most of the dists gain.

RDOQ ±2 candidates, λ=0.054. bpp=0.020213 (under cap), dists=0.119869, score=0.5608. Surprisingly worse than ±1 reference (0.5849). Strong non-linearity between λ=0.053 (dists=0.11905, over cap) and λ=0.054 (dists=0.11987, under cap). Need to fine-tune λ≈0.0535 to hit cap precisely.

RDOQ ±2 candidates, λ=0.0535. bpp=0.02023061 (just under cap 0.02023081), dists=0.118743, score=0.8319. Big improvement over reference (0.585). Fine-tuning λ precisely to the bpp cap was key. Best so far.

Sigma-adaptive RDOQ ±2, α=0.5, λ_base=0.02. bpp=0.02125 OVER cap (0.020231) → score=0. But dists=0.11163 is MUCH better than best (0.11874). Proves sigma-adaptive allocation works - reallocating bits to high-σ coefficients is very efficient for DISTS reduction. Need higher λ_base to bring bpp under control.

Sigma-adaptive RDOQ ±2, α=0.5, λ_base=0.03. bpp=0.02038 OVER cap (0.020231) → score=0. Surprisingly, dists=0.11983 is WORSE than constant-λ best (0.11874 at similar bpp). α=0.5 is too aggressive near the bpp cap: reallocating too many bits to rare high-σ coefficients at the expense of abundant low-σ coefficients. Need smaller α.

Sigma-adaptive RDOQ ±2, α=0.25, λ_base=0.032. bpp=0.02081 OVER cap → score=0. dists=0.11560 is 2.6% better than best valid (0.11874). α=0.25 works better than α=0.5 near the bpp cap (milder reallocation = better overall RD). Need higher λ_base (~0.038) to get under cap.
Sigma-adaptive RDOQ ±2, α=0.25, λ_base=0.038. bpp=0.02041 (0.9% over cap) → score=0. dists=0.11835 is already better than best valid (0.11874). Very close! Need λ_base≈0.041 to get under cap.

Sigma-adaptive RDOQ ±2, α=0.25, λ_base=0.041. bpp=0.020264 (0.000033 over cap = 0.16%) → score=0. dists=0.11830, 0.37% better than best valid (0.11874). Barely over cap, need tiny λ increase to ~0.042.

Sigma-adaptive RDOQ ±2, α=0.25, λ_base=0.042. bpp=0.020242 (barely over cap) but dists=0.12016 JUMPS UP 1.6% from λ=0.041 (0.11830). Severe cliff effect near bpp cap. Need to find sweet spot between λ=0.041 and λ=0.042, or use a different adaptation strategy.

Sigma-adaptive α=0.25, λ_base=0.0415. bpp=0.02025, dists=0.11925. Confirms cliff between λ=0.041 and 0.042: dists rapidly degrades (0.1183→0.1202) while bpp barely changes (0.02026→0.02024). Root cause: high-σ coefficients transition from ±2 to ±1 as λ increases, causing abrupt distortion jump.

Thresholded sigma-adaptive (σ_min=0.2, α=0.5, λ_base=0.03). bpp=0.02039, dists=0.11972. No improvement over smooth sigma-adaptive or constant λ. Current best valid remains constant-λ ±2 RDOQ (score=0.832).

RDOQ ±3 candidates, λ=0.054. bpp=0.020213, dists=0.119869, score=0.5608. IDENTICAL to ±2 at same λ - ±3 candidates never used at this bitrate. Best valid remains constant-λ ±2 at λ=0.0535 (score=0.832).

Mild sigma-adaptive RDOQ ±2, α=0.1, λ_base=0.045. bpp=0.02039 (over cap), dists=0.11830. Promising: RD efficiency is good. Also discovered non-monotonic DISTS vs λ for constant λ (dists minimum at λ≈0.0535) - latent MSE ≠ DISTS. Need to tune λ_base higher to hit cap.

Mild sigma-adaptive RDOQ ±2, α=0.1, λ_base=0.047. bpp=0.020289 (0.29% over cap), dists=0.11793. DISTS is 0.69% better than best valid (0.11874)! DISTS still decreasing as λ increases (non-monotonic pattern). Need λ_base≈0.0485 to hit cap.

Mild sigma-adaptive α=0.1, λ_base=0.0485. bpp=0.020233 (just over cap), dists=0.119335. Worse than best valid (0.11874). DISTS minimum for α=0.1 is at bpp≈0.02029 (above cap). Past the minimum, DISTS increases rapidly as bpp decreases. Need to try smaller α to bring minimum closer to cap.

Very mild sigma-adaptive α=0.05, λ_base=0.050. bpp=0.02028 (over cap), dists=0.11870. Only 0.04% better dists than best valid (0.11874) but with 0.24% more bpp. Very low RD efficiency. Best valid remains constant-λ ±2 at λ=0.0535 (score=0.832).

Inverse sigma-adaptive α=-0.05, λ_base=0.057. bpp=0.02020, dists=0.12029, score=0.460. Much worse than best valid (0.832). Confirms that high-sigma coefficients are perceptually more important - giving them fewer bits hurts DISTS. Best valid remains constant-λ ±2 (score=0.832).

RDOQ ±2 with dead-zone bonus (γ=0.008, λ=0.052). bpp=0.02021, dists=0.11957, score=0.634. Slightly better than constant λ at same bpp (0.56→0.63), but worse than best valid 0.832. Two-parameter approach shows promise but needs tuning at higher bpp.

L1-norm RDOQ ±2, λ=0.035. bpp=0.02115 (over cap), dists=0.11179. EXCELLENT at high bpp - much better than L2 RDOQ. L1 distortion aligns better with DISTS. Need to increase λ to ~0.050 to approach the cap.

L1-norm RDOQ ±2, λ=0.050. bpp=0.02038 (0.74% over cap), dists=0.11804. MATCHES upper bound dists! L1 distortion aligns much better with DISTS than L2. Need λ≈0.055 to hit cap. Best dists achieved so far at this bpp level.

L1-norm RDOQ ±2, λ=0.055. bpp=0.02017 (under cap), dists=0.11993, score=0.546. Worse than L2 best (0.832) at the cap. L1 is much better than L2 at higher bpp (dists=0.11179 at bpp=0.02115) but degrades faster as bpp decreases. L2 wins at the cap because its DISTS optimum falls right at the cap.
L1 RDOQ + mild sigma-adaptive α=0.05, λ_base=0.048. bpp=0.02033 (over cap), dists=0.11812. Similar to pure L1 at comparable bpp. Best valid remains constant-L2 ±2 (score=0.832, dists=0.11874).

Huber loss RDOQ (δ=0.8, λ=0.052). bpp=0.01832, dists=0.14193. Very poor - wrong loss scale, way too few bits. Not a promising direction without extensive tuning. Best valid remains constant-L2 ±2 (score=0.832).

Per-channel-group RDOQ ±2, 4 groups (λ=[0.050,0.052,0.055,0.058]). bpp=0.020191, dists=0.118531, score=0.8831. NEW BEST! Up from 0.832 (constant λ). Earlier channels are perceptually more important - reallocating bits from later to earlier channels improves DISTS.

Per-channel RDOQ ±2, 8 groups (λ=[0.046..0.062] linear). bpp=0.020177, dists=0.118364, score=0.9248. NEW BEST! Up from 0.883 with 4 groups. More groups + steeper ramp = better DISTS. Still ~0.25% bit budget headroom available.

Per-channel RDOQ ±2, 16 groups, curved ramp (t^1.5, λ=0.045→0.063). bpp=0.020220, dists=0.117381, score=1.1599 (clipped=1.0). NEW BEST - beats upper bound! Per-channel allocation with curved ramp is highly effective. ~0.05% bit budget headroom remaining.

Per-channel RDOQ ±2, 32 groups, t^2.0 ramp (λ=0.043→0.065). bpp=0.02029 (over cap), dists=0.11834. Worse than 16-group t^1.5 (0.11738). Too steep an exponent degrades later channels too much. Best remains 16 groups t^1.5 (score=1.16).

Per-channel RDOQ ±2, 16 groups, t^1.5 (λ=0.044→0.064). bpp=0.0202306 (0.001% under cap - nearly perfect!), dists=0.117240, score=1.1936. NEW BEST! Up from 1.16. Fine-tuning lambda range to use all bit budget pays off.

Per-channel 16-group RDOQ + mild sigma-adaptive (α=0.03). bpp=0.02022, dists=0.11794, score=1.026. Worse than pure per-channel (1.194). Sigma-adaptive hurts at the cap - reallocated bits within channels don't improve DISTS as much as across channels. Best remains pure per-channel 16 groups t^1.5 (score=1.194).

Per-channel RDOQ ±2, 16 groups, t^1.2 (λ=0.044→0.066). bpp=0.020135, dists=0.116818, score=1.2953. NEW BEST! Shallower ramp (1.2 vs 1.5) is better - middle channels are more important than previously thought. 0.475% bit budget still unused.

Per-channel RDOQ ±2, 16 groups, linear t^1.0 ramp (λ=0.042→0.068). bpp=0.02008, dists=0.11891, score=0.792. Worse than t^1.2 (1.295). Optimal ramp shape is concave-up with exponent ~1.2. t^1.0 is too flat - early channels under-allocated, late channels over-penalized.

Per-channel RDOQ ±2, 16 groups, t^1.15 (λ=0.043→0.067). bpp=0.020117, dists=0.117647, score=1.0947. Worse than t^1.2 (1.295). Exponent 1.2 is confirmed as the sweet spot between 1.0 (too flat) and 1.5 (too steep).

Per-channel t^1.2 ramp, λ=0.040→0.067 (wider range). bpp=0.020190, dists=0.119240, score=0.712. Worse than t^1.2 0.044→0.066 (score=1.295). Wider ramp hurts DISTS - early channels get too many bits (diminishing returns) and late channels get too few (steep distortion cost). Optimal shape is a mild concave-up curve.

U-shaped per-channel lambda (low in middle, high at ends). bpp=0.02035 (over cap), dists=0.11906. Worse than t^1.2 ramp (score=1.295). Earliest channels are too important to raise lambda. Best remains 16-group t^1.2 (score=1.295).

32 groups per-channel RDOQ, t^1.2 (λ=0.044→0.066). bpp=0.020127, dists=0.117331, score=1.1722. Worse than 16-group t^1.2 (score=1.295). Finer grouping doesn't help and may overfit. Optimal granularity is ~16 groups.

Per-channel RDOQ ±2, 128 groups (per-channel), t^1.2 (λ=0.044→0.066). bpp=0.020129, dists=0.118355, score=0.925. Much worse than 16-group t^1.2 (1.295). Per-channel granularity overfits - 16 groups captures the optimal channel allocation structure.

16-group RDOQ t^1.2, uniformly lower lambda (λ=0.042→0.064). bpp=0.020234 OVER cap (0.020231) → score=0. Surprisingly dists=0.117186 is WORSE than best (0.116818) despite more bits. Extra bits went to early channels (diminishing DISTS returns) while late channels didn't get enough. Uniform lambda shift is bad - need to reallocate across channels.

16-group RDOQ t^1.2, narrower range (λ=0.045→0.064). bpp=0.02018, dists=0.11774, score=1.073. Worse than best (1.295). Reallocating bits from early to late channels hurts DISTS - early channels are more perceptually important than we thought. t^1.2 with 0.044→0.066 remains optimal shape.

16-group RDOQ t^1.2 with CAND_WIDTH=3 (±3 candidates). bpp=0.02014, dists=0.11682, score=1.295. Identical to ±2 version - virtually no coefficients need ±3 quantization. ±2 candidate set is sufficient.
12-group RDOQ t^1.2 (λ=0.044→0.066). bpp=0.02009, dists=0.11799, score=1.013. Worse than 16-group (1.295). Confirms 16 groups is the optimal granularity - 12 is too coarse, 32+ overfits.

16-group t^1.2 RDOQ + per-image adaptive lambda (alpha=0.3, scale-based). bpp=0.02014, dists=0.11682, score=1.295. Identical to baseline - per-image scale variation is too small to matter. Per-image adaptation provides no benefit.

16-group t^1.2 RDOQ with L1 (abs) distortion instead of L2. bpp=0.02013, dists=0.11693, score=1.269. Worse than L2 (1.295). L2 MSE is better aligned with DISTS - small coefficient distortion is perceptually important and shouldn't be aggressively zeroed.

RDOQ with channels sorted by mean scale (descending), 16 groups t^1.2 (λ=0.044→0.066). bpp=0.02067 OVER cap → score=0. But dists=0.11636 is BETTER than best (0.11682)! Scale-sorted allocation is more efficient for distortion - high-σ channels truly need more bits. Need higher lambda to bring bpp under cap.

Scale-sorted RDOQ with higher lambda (0.052→0.078). bpp=0.02029 still OVER cap, dists=0.11809, score=0. Worse DISTS than index-sorted at similar bpp (0.11682 at 0.020135). At low bitrates, channel-index ordering is better than scale ordering - early channels have higher perceptual importance per bit.

16-group t^1.2 RDOQ, narrower range same start (λ=0.044→0.064). bpp=0.02019, dists=0.11800, score=1.011. Worse than best (1.295). Giving late channels more bits (lower lambda) hurts - late channels are truly less perceptually important. t^1.2 0.044→0.066 remains firmly optimal.
16-group RDOQ with exponent 1.22 (λ=0.044→0.066). bpp=0.02014, dists=0.11706, score=1.236. Worse than 1.2 (1.295). Confirms exponent 1.2 is the sweet spot between 1.15 (1.095) and 1.22 (1.236).

16-group t^1.2 RDOQ + perceptual masking (alpha=0.15, high sigma → higher lambda). bpp=0.01975, dists=0.12194, score=0.064. Terrible! Perceptual masking is wrong direction - high-sigma coefficients are MORE perceptually important, not less. Confirms high sigma = high DISTS importance.

16-group t^1.2 RDOQ with L3 (cubed) distortion. bpp=0.01947, dists=0.12587, score=-0.883. Terrible! L3 massively over-penalizes large errors, causing too many zeros and poor quality. L2 is confirmed as far the best distortion norm.

16-group RDOQ with exponent 0.8 (concave-down ramp). bpp=0.02006, dists=0.11880, score=0.819. Much worse than t^1.2 (1.295). Confirms optimal shape is mildly concave-up with exponent ~1.2. Too flat (t^0.8-1.0) and too steep (t^1.5+) are both worse.

16-group t^1.2 RDOQ + spatial gradient (center-biased, 5% strength). bpp=0.02008, dists=0.11844, score=0.904. Worse than baseline (1.295). Spatial reallocation of bits hurts - perceptual importance doesn't vary spatially in the latent space. Per-channel allocation remains the right granularity.

16-group t^1.2 RDOQ with SNR-normalized distortion (MSE/sigma^2). bpp=0.02325 WAY over cap → score=0. But dists=0.10244 is MASSIVELY better than best (0.1168)! SNR-normalized distortion is far more DISTS-efficient - high-sigma coefficients contribute less distortion per unit error. Major discovery! Need higher lambda to bring bpp under cap.
SNR-normalized RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.08→0.12. bpp=0.02271, dists=0.10161, score=0. Still way over cap.
SNR-normalized RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.15→0.22. bpp=0.02182, dists=0.10649, score=0. SNR is efficient at high bitrates.
SNR-normalized RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.25→0.37. bpp=0.02094, dists=0.11638, score=0. Near cap, dists slightly better than MSE (0.1168).
SNR-normalized RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.30→0.44. bpp=0.02060, dists=0.11898, score=0. Below previous but DISTS worse than MSE at cap.
SNR-normalized RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.34→0.50. bpp=0.02033, dists=0.12360, score=0. Near cap but DISTS much worse than MSE.
Sigma-normalized (alpha=1.0) RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.09→0.135. bpp=0.02081, dists=0.11573, score=0. Better DISTS than SNR at similar bpp.
Sigma-normalized (alpha=1.0) RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.11→0.165. bpp=0.02041, dists=0.11927, score=0. DISTS worse than MSE near cap.
Sigma^0.5-normalized (alpha=0.5) RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.055→0.083. bpp=0.02078, dists=0.11487, score=0. Best at ~0.0208 bpp - alpha=0.5 is optimal at medium bitrates.
Sigma^0.5-normalized RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.070→0.105. bpp=0.02024, dists=0.12002, score=0. Near cap but DISTS worse than pure MSE.
Sigma^0.25-normalized (alpha=0.25) RDOQ 16g t^1.2, λ=0.050→0.075. bpp=0.02044, dists=0.11785, score=0. Still worse than MSE at similar bitrate.

16-group t^1.2 RDOQ + mild sigma-adaptive with negative alpha=-0.05 (high-sigma gets lower lambda). bpp=0.02026 over cap, dists=0.11777, score=0. Worse than pure per-channel MSE (0.11682). Sigma-adaptive in either direction hurts at the bpp cap.
